summary: This short program stores an item name and its price in two variables, then uses an f-string to build one sentence that includes both values.

lines.text: A number written with a decimal point is a float, so Python stores 19.99 as a numeric value you could do arithmetic with, not as text.

The f before the opening quote marks this as an f-string: Python replaces each name in braces with that variable's value. Without the f, the output would contain the literal characters {item} and {price}.

The dollar sign here is just an ordinary character in the text; only the braces are special. Note also that the float prints as 19.99 exactly as typed — if you wanted a guaranteed two decimal places, you would ask for {price:.2f}.
